narrative.overview: WordCounter is a quantitative instrument for measuring linguistic production versus recognition. It rejects decorative flashcards, cartoonish mascots, and gamified streaks in favor of high-density, honest lexical accounting. The aesthetic reflects modern developer toolcraft adapted to language learners: calm, precise, and razor-sharp.
keyCharacteristics: Deep zinc void canvas with etched hairline boundaries.
Strict three-tier semantic color coding: Emerald for production (active), Amber for recognition (passive), Indigo for cumulative frequency.
Tabular figures and monospaced data density across all metric displays.
Zero-friction instant interaction with keyboard shortcuts (Cmd+Enter).

rules.name: The Semantic Separation Rule
rules.body: Emerald never represents recognition; Amber never represents production. A word's visual state communicates its cognitive domain instantly across every view.

rules.name: The Contrast Discipline Rule
rules.body: Never place gray text on colored button backgrounds. Always use the dedicated deep-tinted text tokens (#022c22 for emerald, #451a03 for amber).

rules.name: The Tabular Data Rule
rules.body: All numbers, counters, dates, and frequency multipliers must render in monospaced or tabular-figured font to ensure vertical visual stability during live updates.

rules.name: The Tonal Depth Rule
rules.body: Surfaces never cast heavy dark drop shadows. Elevation is achieved through subtle border contrast (border-zinc-800/80) and luminosity contrast between nested backgrounds.

dos: Do allow direct in-memory text analysis immediately on the dashboard landing screen.
Do use text-emerald-950 and text-amber-950 on solid semantic buttons to maintain WCAG AAA contrast.
Do format dates and numbers with monospaced tabular numerals.
Do provide confirmation dialogs before executing bulk destructive actions.
donts: Don't add cartoonish gamification, streaks, confetti, or artificial achievement badges.
Don't use generic gray text on colored status backgrounds.
Don't hide primary input workflows behind extra navigation clicks when they belong in the first viewport.
Don't store or persist raw authored text on disk; token metrics are the only durable domain artifact.
